reproduction: Build the exploratory desktop binary (debug, --no-default-features --features offline) and launch it as an ordinary eframe application with --workspace pointing at a disposable clone of the repository; no --smoke, --beta-smoke, --windowed-e2e or test helper flag is used.
Open README.md from the Explorer drawer, close the drawer, and click the first-line code surface so the accessible text element reports focus.
Type the marker NATIVE_BASELINE_20260905 with native OS key injection; the buffer shows the marker and the tab shows the dirty indicator.
With the reported caret at Ln 1 Col 8, press the OS Home key.
Read the caret position the product reports.
defects.expected: Home moves the caret to the start of the current line and the product reports the new column; End moves it to the end of the line, and the command modifier with Home or End moves to the start or end of the document.
defects.observed: On 2026-09-05, with the caret reported at Ln 1 Col 8 in the open README, the OS Home key did not move the reported cursor at all. A read-only source trace then confirmed the cause: the desktop keyboard path contained no egui::Key::Home or egui::Key::End arm, editor_keyboard_control_actions handled only the arrow and PageUp/PageDown keys, and the code canvas is a custom painter rather than an egui TextEdit, so nothing else could have supplied the mapping. A source fix has since landed in crates/legion-desktop/src/workflow.rs, which now maps Home and End to EditorBoundaryKind::LineStart and LineEnd and, with the command modifier, to DocumentStart and DocumentEnd. No native run has re-observed the key since that change, so the fix is unverified at the product layer.

reproduction: Build the exploratory desktop binary (debug, --no-default-features --features offline) and launch it as an ordinary eframe application with --workspace pointing at a disposable clone of the repository.
Open README.md, click the first-line code surface, and type the marker NATIVE_BASELINE_20260905 with native OS key injection so the tab shows the dirty indicator.
Refresh the window state and read the tab dirty indicator.
From a host shell, read README.md and compute its SHA-256, then run git diff in the clone.
For contrast, open the Command palette, focus its native query edit, type save, wait for the filter to settle so Save Active Buffer is selected, and press Return.
Refresh, read the dirty indicator again, and repeat the host read, hash and git diff.
defects.expected: The OS Control+S chord saves the active buffer through the same authoritative route the Save Active Buffer command uses: the dirty indicator clears and the file on disk changes to contain the typed marker.
defects.observed: On 2026-09-05, after native typing, the injected Control_L+s chord left the dirty indicator set and left the external README bytes unchanged on a subsequent host read. The Command palette route on the same session and the same buffer cleared the dirty indicator and produced a verified on-disk change (README SHA-256 moved from 607892DC8A45879A54B0B3F1BE149A3A28E447090715E9BB24EB14AA2673F2FC to D5D1264A0B0C212A1D74A46279D7AEF99FD97F2CC5AAD42CFA16C6B356459E33, with git diff reporting one addition and one deletion on the first line only). That contrast narrows the failure to shortcut and input ingress rather than the write path. HYPOTHESIS, UNCONFIRMED: the leading explanation is a frame-level egui::Modifiers.command mismatch for an injected Control_L+s, because the desktop dispatcher qualifies a key event with the frame-level modifier state rather than the event-time modifiers. No native event log capturing the actual egui::InputState.modifiers or Event::Key fields for that chord exists, so the cause is not established and no source defect is asserted here. Automation-tool and desktop-focus interference events were observed in the same session and are deliberately excluded; they are not product behaviour.

reproduction: Prerequisites: the retained fixture .superpowers/sdd/2026-09-04-full-product-completion/pyright-1.1.400.tgz, and LEGION_TEST_NODE_RUNTIME set to an absolute Node executable, as crates/legion-app/tests/python_app_startup.rs requires. The transcripts record only the CMD line, so the exact Node executable used in the four r08 runs is not recoverable from them.

On an otherwise idle Windows 11 x64 host, from the repository root, run: cargo test -p legion-app --test typescript_app_startup --test python_app_startup -j 1 --no-fail-fast -- --ignored --nocapture. Transcript .superpowers/sdd/2026-09-04-full-product-completion/round-r08-test-s2-02a-live-language-servers.log records `test result: ok. 4 passed; 0 failed` for python_app_startup in 23.47s, `test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed` for typescript_app_startup in 17.76s, and `EXIT=0`.

Load the host: start the MSI package build and leave it competing for CPU and disk. No transcript records the load; it is carried from the round-r08 lane record as an operator observation of when the next two runs were taken, and no host CPU or IO measurement was captured.

Under that load, re-run the same command. Transcript round-r08-fixtest1-s2-02a-fix1-tests.log records `test result: FAILED. 1 passed; 3 failed` for python_app_startup in 16.39s, with native_python_diagnostic_clears_after_editor_replace_and_save the only survivor, `test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed` for typescript_app_startup in 23.17s, and `EXIT=101`.

Still under that load, remove test parallelism: cargo test -p legion-app --test python_app_startup -j 1 --no-fail-fast -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1. Transcript round-r08-fixtest1-s2-02a-fix1-tests-python-serial.log records `test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 4 failed` in 37.50s and `EXIT=101`. Serializing removed the survivor rather than the failure.

Stop the MSI build, let the host settle to idle, and run: cargo test -p legion-app --test python_app_startup -j 1 --no-fail-fast -- --ignored --nocapture. Transcript round-r08-post-python-idle.log records `test result: ok. 4 passed; 0 failed` in 24.53s and `EXIT=0`.
Read the failure text in either failing transcript. Host load is the only variable that changed across the four runs: same workspace, same fixture, same test binaries, same command shape.
defects.expected: When a language-server startup fails because a bounded host-side operation ran out of its finite deadline, the product must report that failure for what it is - a transient host condition that prevented the server from starting - and must not tell the operator that the launch configuration is invalid when every configured input validated: the operator-selected Node path canonicalized, the capability broker granted the probe, and the retained artifact materialized before the probe was reached. The session must also be allowed to spend the automatic-restart budget it advertises (max_auto_restarts) with its configured backoff before the startup is presented as terminal, because a condition that clears on an idle host is exactly the condition that budget exists for. Which mechanism delivers that - a distinct transient error variant, a different classification at the conversion site, a per-phase rather than shared budget, or a different budget value - is the repair packet's decision under repair_package_id S2-02 and is deliberately not prescribed here.
defects.observed: SCOPE: this is component-layer evidence only. All four runs were the in-process integration test crates/legion-app/tests/python_app_startup.rs driving legion_app::AppComposition::new() directly (crates/legion-app/tests/python_app_startup.rs:219, :325, :454, :517). No packaged product was built, no window was created, and no native input was injected. CFG-WIN11-X64-PY-APP is recorded here as the NEAREST REGISTER CELL for the Windows 11 x64 Python-application shape (plans/completion/matrix.json project_category `python-application-isolated`); it is not a claim that a packaged-product or product-journey run observed this, and it must not be read as one. FAILURE TEXT, verbatim from .superpowers/sdd/2026-09-04-full-product-completion/round-r08-fixtest1-s2-02a-fix1-tests-python-serial.log, identical in all four failing cases there and in the three failing cases of round-r08-fixtest1-s2-02a-fix1-tests.log: assertion `left != right` failed: Pyright startup was refused: status=LspSessionStatusProjection { lifecycle: Refused, restart_count: 0, max_auto_restarts: 3, backoff_remaining_ms: None, failure_reason: Some("language-server launch configuration is invalid: Node executable identity check timed out"), schema_version: 1 }, health=Some(LspServerHealthRecord { server_id: LanguageServerId(104), language_id: LanguageId("python"), binary_provenance: Downloaded, binary_path_hash: None, artifact_hash: None, version: None, init_status: Unavailable, capabilities: [], diagnostics_latency_ms: None, restart_count: 0, download_decision_id: None, schema_version: 1 }), stderr=None. SOURCE CHAIN, every anchor read in this workspace at commit 51af391a45d33cf15a359c1e4b91bc314d768cde: (1) crates/legion-app/src/language/runtime.rs:56 defines `pub(crate) const EXECUTABLE_PROBE_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(5);`, re-exported at runtime.rs:46 as NODE_RUNTIME_PROBE_TIMEOUT, whose doc comment at runtime.rs:44-45 states that hashing, broker evaluation and the child probe share this budget and the child receives only the remaining duration; approve_node_runtime derives one deadline for all three phases at runtime.rs:208. (2) Exceeding it yields NodeRuntimeApprovalError::DeadlineExceeded, declared at runtime.rs:169-170 as `#[error("Node executable identity check timed out")]`, reached either from ExecutableIdentityError::DeadlineExceeded (runtime.rs:182) or from BoundedProbeError::DeadlineExceeded (runtime.rs:244). (3) CONVERSION SITE, located by reading the source rather than taken from the packet brief: crates/legion-app/src/language/startup_authority.rs:495-501, inside `prepare_downloaded_local` (declared at startup_authority.rs:428), calls `super::approve_node_runtime(...)` and discards the error class with `.map_err(|error| invalid(error.to_string()))?` at startup_authority.rs:501, where the helper `invalid` at startup_authority.rs:727-729 is `LanguageSessionError::InvalidConfiguration(message.into())`. That is the path this test takes: the test calls AppComposition::configure_downloaded_language_server_local (crates/legion-app/src/lib.rs:16687), which stores a LanguageStartupSelection::DownloadedLocal (crates/legion-app/src/lib.rs:17444) dispatched to prepare_downloaded_local at crates/legion-app/src/lib.rs:17165. A structurally identical sibling conversion sits at startup_authority.rs:139-145 in `prepare_typescript_bundle`, so the misclassification is shared code and not Python-specific. (4) Display at crates/legion-app/src/language/session.rs:75-77 renders `language-server launch configuration is invalid: {e}`, which is the string in the log. (5) RESTART BUDGET: crates/legion-app/src/language/app_lsp.rs:902-905 matches LanguageSessionError::InvalidConfiguration and assigns LspSessionState::Refused directly, returning before the else arm at app_lsp.rs:915-917 that calls transition_failure - and transition_failure (app_lsp.rs:932-946) is the only code that increments restart_count and schedules BackingOff. LspSessionState::Refused is documented at app_lsp.rs:395 as `Launch was refused (untrusted, no binary, policy denied, etc.)` and is treated as terminal by is_refused_or_failed at app_lsp.rs:473-478; its projection at app_lsp.rs:544-551 carries restart_count unchanged and backoff_remaining_ms None, exactly matching the logged projection. The misclassification therefore does more than word the failure badly: it routes the startup around the three automatic restarts the same projection advertises. BOUND: typescript_app_startup passed 6 of 6 in every run, including both loaded ones (round-r08-fixtest1-s2-02a-fix1-tests.log records `test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed` in 23.17s in the same loaded window that failed 3 of 4 Python cases). The observed deadline overrun is thus bound to the Python/Pyright DownloadedLocal approval probe in these four runs and is not evidence of a general language-session failure; because the sibling conversion at startup_authority.rs:145 is the same shape, that bound applies to the timeout, not to the misclassification. HYPOTHESIS, UNCONFIRMED: whether the 5s budget was consumed by the bounded identity hash of the Node executable, by capability-broker evaluation, or by the child probe is not established by any log in hand - no per-phase timing was captured, and nothing here asserts one. HYPOTHESIS, UNCONFIRMED: attributing the two failing runs to concurrent MSI-build load rests on the operator's record of when they were taken, not on any captured host CPU or IO measurement. SEVERITY ARGUMENT: P2. COMP-LANG-010 requires `unavailable-server failures truthful`, and the reported reason is untruthful about both the cause (the configuration validated; the host was busy) and the permanence (a self-clearing condition presented as a refusal with the restart budget unspent), so this is more than cosmetic and is not P3. It sits below the two P1 rows in this register, which are unconditional product-layer breakages of a basic keystroke path that reproduce at rest; this one did not reproduce on an idle host in two of four runs, substitutes nothing, loses no data, presents no wrong result as right, and leaves a manual restart available - so it is neither P1 nor P0. INVALIDATION ARGUMENT: invalidates_required_outcome is true. The required outcome in COMP-LANG-010 is not `the server usually starts` but `unavailable-server failures truthful`; a build shipping this behaviour tells an operator on a loaded machine to go repair a configuration that is correct and then never retries, which contradicts that required text rather than merely degrading it. The counter-argument - that the condition is load-dependent and two runs passed - would be decisive if the requirement were about availability, and it is not: intermittency changes how often the untruthful message is produced, not whether the product produces it. CONSEQUENCE, ACKNOWLEDGED: with this flag true and status open, xtask/src/completion_command.rs:237-242 makes release-mode validation emit `release has unresolved defect DEF-0003 invalidating a required outcome` and fail, while development mode tolerates it; xtask/tests/completion_command.rs:312-333 asserts exactly that pair of behaviours. Release is therefore blocked on this row until a repair under S2-02 closes it against a passing verification run.
